entries.contrast: Not all students agreed with the proposal. · None of the students agreed with the proposal.

question.zh-Hans: 一句话会暗含未说出的前提吗？
question.zh-Hant: 一句話會暗含未說出的前提嗎？
question.en: Can wording presuppose an unstated fact?

summary.zh-Hans: stop、still、even 等词常带出超出字面断言的背景信息。
summary.zh-Hant: stop、still、even 等詞常帶出超出字面斷言的背景資訊。
summary.en: Words such as stop, still and even often introduce background assumptions beyond the main assertion.

usage.zh-Hans: She stopped smoking 通常预设她过去吸烟；She still works here 暗示原本可能预期她已离开；Even Jo passed 暗示 Jo 通过考试在某个比较尺度上出人意料。预设会受语境、否定和纠正影响，不能当作已验证事实。
usage.zh-Hant: She stopped smoking 通常預設她過去吸菸；She still works here 暗示原本可能預期她已離開；Even Jo passed 暗示 Jo 通過考試在某個比較尺度上出乎意料。預設會受語境、否定和糾正影響，不能當作已驗證事實。
usage.en: She stopped smoking normally presupposes prior smoking; She still works here suggests continued employment against a possible expectation; Even Jo passed frames Jo’s success as surprising on some scale. Context, negation and correction can affect these inferences; they are not verified facts.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 引述他人“仍然”“终于”时，先辨认这些词是谁的预设，避免把它写成自己的证据结论。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 引述他人「仍然」「終於」時，先辨認這些詞是誰的預設，避免把它寫成自己的證據結論。
pitfall.en: When quoting still or finally, identify whose assumption it conveys before presenting it as your own evidence.

entries.pattern: stop + -ing · still + verb · even + focused item
entries.example: She stopped calling after June.
examples: She stopped calling after June.
He still works here.
Even the shortest route took two hours.
entries.contrast: She stopped calling after June. · He still works here.

question.zh-Hans: It was ... that 强调什么？
question.zh-Hant: It was ... that 強調什麼？
question.en: What does It was ... that focus?

summary.zh-Hans: It-cleft 把一个成分标为焦点，并把其余信息置于背景。
summary.zh-Hant: It-cleft 把一個成分標為焦點，並把其餘資訊置於背景。
summary.en: An it-cleft presents one constituent as focus and treats the remaining proposition as background.

usage.zh-Hans: It was Maya who found the error 强调发现者是 Maya；It was the error that Maya found 强调被发现的对象。使用时要检查焦点是否回答了实际争议，否则读者可能误会作者在纠正哪一项。常见关联词有 who、that。
usage.zh-Hant: It was Maya who found the error 強調發現者是 Maya；It was the error that Maya found 強調被發現的對象。使用時要檢查焦點是否回應了實際爭議，否則讀者可能誤會作者在糾正哪一項。常見關聯詞有 who、that。
usage.en: It was Maya who found the error focuses on the finder; It was the error that Maya found focuses on the object found. Check that the focus answers the actual dispute, or readers may misunderstand what is being corrected. Who and that are common linkers.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要把每个 it was ... that 都当作普通“它是”；这里的 it 通常不是具体事物的代词。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要把每個 it was ... that 都當作一般的「它是」；這裡的 it 通常不是具體事物的代名詞。
pitfall.en: Do not interpret every cleft it as referring to a concrete object.

entries.pattern: It + be + focus + that/who + remainder
entries.example: It was Maya who found the error.
examples: It was Maya who found the error.
It was the error that Maya found.
It is the timing that worries me.
entries.contrast: It was Maya who found the error. · It was the error that Maya found.

question.zh-Hans: only 放在哪里会改变意思？
question.zh-Hant: only 放在哪裡會改變意思？
question.en: How does only change meaning by position?

summary.zh-Hans: only 限制其所聚焦的成分；位置和语调会改变读者理解。
summary.zh-Hant: only 限制其所聚焦的成分；位置和語調會改變讀者理解。
summary.en: Only limits the focused constituent; position and stress can change the interpretation.

usage.zh-Hans:
Only Sara reviewed the draft 表示其他人没有审阅；Sara only reviewed the draft 可能表示她只做了审阅，没修改。书面语缺少语调，正式写作应把 only 尽量放近需要限制的部分，并用上下文消除歧义。

only 的位置通常提示被限定的成分：Only Nora sent the draft 限定发送者；Nora sent only the draft 限定发送的东西；Nora only sent the draft 有时可表示她“只是发送”，但口语重音和语境仍可改变理解。正式写作如果歧义会影响论点，应把 only 紧贴目标成分，必要时重写整个句子。不要只按词序断言某个解释永远唯一。
usage.zh-Hant:
Only Sara reviewed the draft 表示其他人沒有審閱；Sara only reviewed the draft 可能表示她只做了審閱，沒有修改。書面語缺少語調，正式寫作應把 only 盡量放近需要限制的部分，並用上下文消除歧義。

only 的位置通常提示被限定的成分：Only Nora sent the draft 限定寄送者；Nora sent only the draft 限定寄送的東西；Nora only sent the draft 有時可表示她「只是寄送」，但口語重音和語境仍可改變理解。正式寫作若歧義會影響論點，應把 only 緊貼目標成分，必要時重寫整句。不要只依詞序斷言某個解釋永遠唯一。
usage.en:
Only Sara reviewed the draft excludes other reviewers. Sara only reviewed the draft may say she reviewed but did not edit it. Written prose lacks spoken stress; place only near the intended focus and use context to remove ambiguity.

Placement usually signals scope: Only Nora sent the draft restricts the sender; Nora sent only the draft restricts the item; Nora only sent the draft may mean she merely sent it. Stress and context can still change spoken interpretation. In precise writing, place only beside the intended element and rewrite if the distinction affects the argument. Word order alone does not guarantee a unique reading in every context.

pitfall.zh-Hans: Sara reviewed only the draft 不等于 Only Sara reviewed the draft；前者限制审阅对象。
pitfall.zh-Hant: Sara reviewed only the draft 不等於 Only Sara reviewed the draft；前者限制審閱對象。
pitfall.en: Sara reviewed only the draft limits the object, not the people who reviewed it.

entries.pattern: only + focused person/object/action
entries.example: Only Sara reviewed the draft.
examples: Only Sara reviewed the draft.
Sara only reviewed the draft.
Sara reviewed only the draft.
Only Nora reviewed the draft.
entries.contrast: Only Sara reviewed the draft. · Sara only reviewed the draft.

question.zh-Hans: because 和 because of 后面接什么？
question.zh-Hant: because 和 because of 後面接什麼？
question.en: What follows because and because of?

summary.zh-Hans: because 后接有主语和谓语的分句；because of 后接名词性成分。
summary.zh-Hant: because 後接有主詞和謂語的子句；because of 後接名詞性成分。
summary.en: Because introduces a clause; because of introduces a noun phrase.

usage.zh-Hans: 选择时先看原因本身怎样表达：the road was closed 是分句，接 because；the road closure 是名词短语，接 because of。原因分句放句首时，通常在主句前加逗号；放句末时通常不加。because of 后也可接代词或 -ing 结构，但后者要能当名词性成分理解。两者可以表达相近的原因，句法结构却不能直接互换。
usage.zh-Hant: 選擇時先看原因本身怎樣表達：the road was closed 是子句，接 because；the road closure 是名詞片語，接 because of。原因子句放句首時，通常在主句前加逗號；放句末時通常不加。because of 後也可接代名詞或 -ing 結構，但後者要能當名詞性成分理解。兩者可以表達相近的原因，句法結構卻不能直接互換。
usage.en: Inspect the form of the reason: the road was closed is a clause after because; the road closure is a noun phrase after because of. A reason clause at the beginning is normally followed by a comma, while a final one normally is not. Because of can also take a pronoun or a nominal -ing phrase. Similar reasons can be expressed with either form, but the grammar after them differs.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 because of the road was closed；这里应删去 of，或把原因改成 the road closure。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 because of the road was closed；這裡應刪去 of，或把原因改成 the road closure。
pitfall.en: Avoid because of the road was closed; remove of or change the reason into a noun phrase.

entries.pattern: because + clause · because of + noun phrase
entries.example: The visit ended early because the road was closed.
examples: The visit ended early because the road was closed.
The visit ended early because of the road closure.
Because the lift was broken, we took the stairs.
They changed the route because of heavy rain.
entries.contrast: We stayed inside because it rained. · We stayed inside because of the rain.

question.zh-Hans: 间接问句为什么不用直接问句语序？
question.zh-Hant: 間接問句為什麼不用直接問句語序？
question.en: Why does an indirect question use statement order?

summary.zh-Hans: 嵌入在另一句中的问句通常用主语在动词前的语序；是非问句用 if 或 whether 引入。
summary.zh-Hant: 嵌入在另一句中的問句通常用主詞在動詞前的語序；是非問句用 if 或 whether 引入。
summary.en: An embedded question normally has statement word order; yes–no questions use if or whether.

usage.zh-Hans: 直接问句 Where does the bus stop? 变成 Do you know where the bus stops? 时，where 后不再保留 does + 主语的倒装。原句若用 did 提问，嵌入后仍要表达过去时间，但不保留助动词 did。礼貌请求可以用 Could you tell me...；若整句是疑问句，末尾用问号；I wonder... 是陈述句，通常用句号。无疑问词的是非问句使用 if 或 whether，后面同样用陈述语序。
usage.zh-Hant: 直接問句 Where does the bus stop? 變成 Do you know where the bus stops? 時，where 後不再保留 does + 主詞的倒裝。原句若用 did 提問，嵌入後仍要表達過去時間，但不保留助動詞 did。禮貌請求可以用 Could you tell me...；若整句是疑問句，末尾用問號；I wonder... 是陳述句，通常用句號。無疑問詞的是非問句使用 if 或 whether，後面同樣用陳述語序。
usage.en: When Where does the bus stop? becomes Do you know where the bus stops?, the embedded part loses do-support and inversion. With a past-time question, keep the past meaning but not the question auxiliary did. Could you tell me...? is a polite question and takes a question mark; I wonder... is a statement and normally takes a full stop. For an embedded yes–no question, introduce the clause with if or whether and keep statement order.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 Could you tell me where does the bus stop?；只有外层问句需要倒装。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 Could you tell me where does the bus stop?；只有外層問句需要倒裝。
pitfall.en: Avoid Could you tell me where does the bus stop? Only the outer question is inverted.

entries.pattern: Do you know + question word + subject + verb?
entries.example: Could you tell me where the bus stops?
examples: Could you tell me where the bus stops?
I wonder why the office closed early.
Do you know whether the library is open?
She asked how much the ticket cost.
entries.contrast: Where did they go? · Do you know where they went?

question.zh-Hans: either 和 neither 表示两个选项时怎样用？
question.zh-Hant: either 和 neither 表示兩個選項時怎樣用？
question.en: How do either and neither refer to two alternatives?

summary.zh-Hans: either 表示两者中的任意一个；neither 表示两者都不。either...or 连接选择，neither...nor 同时否定两项。
summary.zh-Hant: either 表示兩者中的任意一個；neither 表示兩者都不。either...or 連接選擇，neither...nor 同時否定兩項。
summary.en: Either means one of two; neither means not one and not the other. Either...or offers alternatives, while neither...nor rejects both.

usage.zh-Hans: 单独作限定词时，either/neither 后接单数可数名词：either route、neither answer。接特定的复数名词或代词时用 either/neither of：neither of the routes、either of us。作主语时，正式写作通常配单数动词；日常口语中的复数动词也可见，不能简单判作绝对错误。either...or / neither...nor 连接的成分应尽量平行；复合主语的动词一致还受最近主语和文体影响。
usage.zh-Hant: 單獨作限定詞時，either/neither 後接單數可數名詞：either route、neither answer。接特定的複數名詞或代名詞時用 either/neither of：neither of the routes、either of us。作主詞時，正式寫作通常配單數動詞；日常口語中的複數動詞也可見，不能簡單判作絕對錯誤。either...or / neither...nor 連接的成分應盡量平行；複合主詞的動詞一致還受最近主詞和文體影響。
usage.en: As determiners, either and neither precede a singular count noun: either route, neither answer. Use either/neither of before a determiner plus plural noun or a pronoun: neither of the routes, either of us. Formal writing commonly uses a singular verb with these as subjects; plural agreement also occurs in informal speech, so it is not an absolute error. Keep the paired elements in either...or and neither...nor parallel. Agreement with a compound subject can depend on the nearer element and style.

pitfall.zh-Hans: neither 已含否定意义，通常不要再给同一意思加 not。涉及三项及以上时，也不要机械地把 neither 当作 none。
pitfall.zh-Hant: neither 已含否定意義，通常不要再給同一意思加 not。涉及三項及以上時，也不要機械地把 neither 當作 none。
pitfall.en: Neither is already negative; do not add not to express the same negation. For three or more items, do not automatically use neither in place of none.

entries.pattern: either + singular noun · neither of + determiner + plural noun
entries.example: Either entrance will take you to the hall.
examples: Either entrance will take you to the hall.
Neither answer explains the delay.
Neither of the two maps shows the new road.
You can email either the editor or the designer.
entries.contrast: Either plan is possible. · Neither plan is possible.

question.zh-Hans: unless 能否直接代替 if not？
question.zh-Hant: unless 能否直接代替 if not？
question.en: Can unless always replace if not?

summary.zh-Hans: unless 常表示“除非”；它适合提出使主句不成立的例外条件，但不能机械替换所有 if not。
summary.zh-Hant: unless 常表示「除非」；它適合提出使主句不成立的例外條件，但不能機械替換所有 if not。
summary.en: Unless often means except if; it introduces an exception, but does not replace every if not clause.

usage.zh-Hans: You cannot enter unless you have a pass 表示“有通行证”是不能进入的例外。谈未来条件时，unless 分句通常用现在时而不是 will。若 if not 是对一个否定事实进行推理或表示“是否不”，改成 unless 往往改变焦点；若想说“如果他不喜欢茶”，也需根据上下文判断究竟是开放条件还是唯一例外。unless 本身含否定条件的意思，不要再随意加 not 造成意义反转。
usage.zh-Hant: You cannot enter unless you have a pass 表示「有通行證」是不能進入的例外。談未來條件時，unless 子句通常用現在式而不是 will。若 if not 是對一個否定事實進行推理或表示「是否不」，改成 unless 往往改變焦點；若想說「如果他不喜歡茶」，也需依上下文判斷究竟是開放條件還是唯一例外。unless 本身含否定條件的意思，不要再隨意加 not 造成意義反轉。
usage.en: You cannot enter unless you have a pass presents having a pass as the exception to a ban. In future-oriented conditions, the unless clause normally uses a present form rather than will. If not can merely state a negative condition or introduce a question about whether something is not true; replacing it with unless may change the focus. Check whether the clause really identifies the only exception. Unless already carries a negative conditional meaning, so another not may reverse the intended sense.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要把 unless 理解为“如果”；也不要在普通未来条件中写 unless you will have a pass。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要把 unless 理解為「如果」；也不要在一般未來條件中寫 unless you will have a pass。
pitfall.en: Do not read unless as a neutral if, or normally write unless you will have a pass for a future condition.

entries.pattern: main clause + unless + present clause
entries.example: The room stays locked unless a guide is present.
examples: The room stays locked unless a guide is present.
Unless the weather improves, we will meet indoors.
I will keep the receipt unless you need it.
We cannot begin unless everyone is ready.
entries.contrast: We will leave if it does not rain. · We will leave unless it rains.

question.zh-Hans: during 和 while 后面分别接什么？
question.zh-Hant: during 和 while 後面分別接什麼？
question.en: What follows during and while?

summary.zh-Hans: during 后接名词性时间段；while 后通常接有主语和动词的分句。
summary.zh-Hant: during 後接名詞性的時段；while 後通常接有主詞和動詞的子句。
summary.en: During takes a noun phrase naming a period; while normally introduces a clause.

usage.zh-Hans: during the meeting 与 while we were meeting 可以描述同一时间关系，但后面的结构不同。during 可以指事件过程中的某一点或贯穿整个时段，具体由语境决定。while 常突出两件事同时发生，也可以表示对比；当两个分句主语相同且意思清楚时，可以省去主语和 be，形成 while waiting 等缩减结构。选词前先看后面是名词短语还是完整分句。
usage.zh-Hant: during the meeting 與 while we were meeting 可以描述同一時間關係，但後面的結構不同。during 可以指事件過程中的某一點或貫穿整個時段，具體由語境決定。while 常凸顯兩件事同時發生，也可以表示對比；當兩個子句主詞相同且意思清楚時，可以省去主詞和 be，形成 while waiting 等簡縮結構。選詞前先看後面是名詞片語還是完整子句。
usage.en: During the meeting and while we were meeting can describe the same period, but the following structures differ. During can mean at some point in an event or throughout it, depending on context. While often highlights simultaneous actions and can also signal contrast. When the subject is shared and clear, a reduced clause such as while waiting is possible. First check whether the following material is a noun phrase or a clause.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 during we waited；可改为 while we waited 或 during the wait。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 during we waited；可改為 while we waited 或 during the wait。
pitfall.en: Avoid during we waited; use while we waited or during the wait.

entries.pattern: during + noun phrase · while + clause
entries.example: The lights went out during the meeting.
examples: The lights went out during the meeting.
The lights went out while we were meeting.
She read the instructions while I checked the map.
Do not use your phone while driving.
entries.contrast: during the flight · while the plane was flying

question.zh-Hans: like 和 as 在比较与身份说明中有何不同？
question.zh-Hant: like 和 as 在比較與身分說明中有何不同？
question.en: How do like and as differ in comparisons and roles?

summary.zh-Hans: like 通常表示“像”；as 可表示“作为某种身份或用途”，也可引出比较分句。
summary.zh-Hant: like 通常表示「像」；as 可表示「以某種身分或用途」，也可引出比較子句。
summary.en: Like commonly means similar to; as can identify a role or function and can introduce a comparison clause.

usage.zh-Hans: She works as a guide 表示她确实担任导览员；She talks like a guide 只描述说话方式相似。比较后若有完整分句，正式写作常用 as：Do it as I showed you；口语中 like + 分句也常见，不宜一概说错。as 还可以引出原因或时间分句，必须结合上下文判断；like 后接名词或代词表示相似，是最稳妥的基本用法。
usage.zh-Hant: She works as a guide 表示她確實擔任導覽員；She talks like a guide 只描述說話方式相似。比較後若有完整子句，正式寫作常用 as：Do it as I showed you；口語中 like + 子句也常見，不宜一概說錯。as 還可以引出原因或時間子句，必須依上下文判斷；like 後接名詞或代名詞表示相似，是最穩妥的基本用法。
usage.en: She works as a guide states her actual role; she talks like a guide describes a resemblance. Before a full comparison clause, formal writing often prefers as: Do it as I showed you. Like plus a clause is also common in speech and should not be labelled universally wrong. As can additionally introduce reason or time clauses, so context matters. Like before a noun or pronoun is the straightforward way to mark resemblance.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要把 work like a guide 与 work as a guide 当作完全同义：前者说“像”，后者说“担任”。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要把 work like a guide 與 work as a guide 當作完全同義：前者說「像」，後者說「擔任」。
pitfall.en: Work like a guide and work as a guide differ: the first compares, the second names a role.

entries.pattern: like + noun/pronoun · as + role · as + clause
entries.example: Mina works as an editor.
examples: Mina works as an editor.
Mina writes like an editor.
Arrange the chairs as we discussed.
This cloth can be used as a cover.
entries.contrast: He acts like a teacher. · He works as a teacher.

question.zh-Hans: stop doing 与 stop to do 为什么意思不同？
question.zh-Hant: stop doing 與 stop to do 為什麼意思不同？
question.en: Why do stop doing and stop to do mean different things?

summary.zh-Hans: stop doing 是停止某个活动；stop to do 是暂停原活动，转而做另一件事。
summary.zh-Hant: stop doing 是停止某項活動；stop to do 是暫停原活動，轉而做另一件事。
summary.en: Stop doing ends an activity; stop to do pauses one activity in order to do another.

usage.zh-Hans: She stopped reading 表示阅读停止了；She stopped to read 表示她停下原先在做的事，目的是阅读。to read 在后一句中表示目的，而不是 stop 的被停止对象。stop somebody from doing something 则表示阻止某人做某事，from 后接 -ing。写句子时先明确“停止的是什么”，再选结构。
usage.zh-Hant: She stopped reading 表示閱讀停止了；She stopped to read 表示她停下原先在做的事，目的是閱讀。to read 在後一句中表示目的，而不是 stop 的被停止對象。stop somebody from doing something 則表示阻止某人做某事，from 後接 -ing。寫句子時先明確「停止的是什麼」，再選結構。
usage.en: She stopped reading says the reading ended. She stopped to read says she paused a different activity for the purpose of reading; to read states purpose, not the activity discontinued. Stop somebody from doing something means prevent an action, with -ing after from. Identify what actually stopped before choosing the pattern.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 要表达“戒烟”用 stop smoking；stop to smoke 表示停下来抽烟，意思几乎相反。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 要表達「戒菸」用 stop smoking；stop to smoke 表示停下來抽菸，意思幾乎相反。
pitfall.en: For giving up smoking, use stop smoking; stop to smoke means pause to have a smoke.

entries.pattern: stop + -ing · stop + to-infinitive · stop someone from + -ing
entries.example: We stopped working when the alarm sounded.
examples: We stopped working when the alarm sounded.
We stopped to check the map.
A fence stopped visitors from crossing the field.
He stopped talking to listen to the announcement.
entries.contrast: She stopped reading. · She stopped to read.

question.zh-Hans: remember doing 和 remember to do 有什么差别？
question.zh-Hant: remember doing 和 remember to do 有什麼差別？
question.en: What is the difference between remember doing and remember to do?

summary.zh-Hans: remember doing 是记得做过的事；remember to do 是记住要做的事。
summary.zh-Hant: remember doing 是記得做過的事；remember to do 是記住要做的事。
summary.en: Remember doing recalls a completed event; remember to do means not forgetting a task.

usage.zh-Hans: I remember locking the door 回顾一个已经发生的动作；I remembered to lock the door 表示当时没有忘记这项任务，并做了它。否定句也不同：I do not remember locking it 是没有这段记忆，不一定证明没锁；I did not remember to lock it 通常表示忘了去锁。forget doing 与 forget to do 有类似的时间和意义区别，但 forget doing 的具体语境需另行判断。
usage.zh-Hant: I remember locking the door 回顧一個已經發生的動作；I remembered to lock the door 表示當時沒有忘記這項任務，並做了它。否定句也不同：I do not remember locking it 是沒有這段記憶，不一定證明沒鎖；I did not remember to lock it 通常表示忘了去鎖。forget doing 與 forget to do 有類似的時間和意義區別，但 forget doing 的具體語境需另行判斷。
usage.en: I remember locking the door looks back at an event. I remembered to lock the door says the task was not forgotten and was carried out. Negation matters: I do not remember locking it reports a missing memory, not proof that it stayed unlocked; I did not remember to lock it normally reports a forgotten task. Forget doing and forget to do show a related contrast, though their exact contexts still need checking.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要用 I remember to lock it 表达“我记得自己锁过”；应说 I remember locking it。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要用 I remember to lock it 表達「我記得自己鎖過」；應說 I remember locking it。
pitfall.en: For a memory of having locked it, say I remember locking it, not I remember to lock it.

entries.pattern: remember + -ing (past event) · remember + to-infinitive (task)
entries.example: I remember meeting her at the station.
examples: I remember meeting her at the station.
Please remember to bring your ticket.
He remembered to save the document.
I cannot remember sending that message.
entries.contrast: I remember posting the letter. · I remembered to post the letter.

question.zh-Hans: suggest 后面能直接接人加不定式吗？
question.zh-Hant: suggest 後面能直接接人加不定詞嗎？
question.en: Can suggest take a person plus to-infinitive?

summary.zh-Hans: 提出建议时常用 suggest + -ing 或 suggest that + 分句；不要按 tell 的句型直接写 suggest someone to do。
summary.zh-Hant: 提出建議時常用 suggest + -ing 或 suggest that + 子句；不要依 tell 的句型直接寫 suggest someone to do。
summary.en: For proposals, use suggest + -ing or suggest that + clause; not the tell pattern suggest someone to do.

usage.zh-Hans: I suggest leaving early 表示建议早出发；I suggest that we leave early 明确指出由谁执行。正式英语中 that 分句可用原形动词；日常英语也可用普通时态形式。suggest 后可以接名词作建议内容，如 suggest a date；若要说明建议对象，可说 suggest to someone that...，而不是把 someone 直接放在 to-infinitive 前。suggest 还可表示“暗示”，此时不能把每个用法都理解成提出建议。
usage.zh-Hant: I suggest leaving early 表示建議早出發；I suggest that we leave early 明確指出由誰執行。正式英語中 that 子句可用原形動詞；日常英語也可用一般時態形式。suggest 後可以接名詞作建議內容，如 suggest a date；若要說明建議對象，可說 suggest to someone that...，而不是把 someone 直接放在 to-infinitive 前。suggest 還可表示「暗示」，此時不能把每個用法都理解成提出建議。
usage.en: I suggest leaving early proposes an action; I suggest that we leave early names the actor. Formal English may use a plain verb form in the that-clause; ordinary tense forms also occur. Suggest can take a noun naming the proposal, as in suggest a date. To name the recipient, say suggest to someone that..., rather than putting the person before a to-infinitive. Suggest can also mean indicate indirectly, where it is not a proposal at all.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 She suggested me to call；可说 She suggested that I call 或 She suggested calling。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 She suggested me to call；可說 She suggested that I call 或 She suggested calling。
pitfall.en: Avoid She suggested me to call; use She suggested that I call or She suggested calling.

entries.pattern: suggest + -ing · suggest (that) + subject + verb
entries.example: I suggest checking the address first.
examples: I suggest checking the address first.
She suggested that we take a later train.
The tutor suggested a shorter title.
The figures suggest that demand is falling.
entries.contrast: She suggested calling. · She told me to call.

question.zh-Hans: needn’t 与 mustn’t 都是否定，为什么意思不同？
question.zh-Hant: needn’t 與 mustn’t 都是否定，為何意思不同？
question.en: Why do needn’t and mustn’t differ?

summary.zh-Hans: needn’t 表示没有必要；mustn’t 表示禁止或强烈要求不要做。
summary.zh-Hant: needn’t 表示沒有必要；mustn’t 表示禁止或強烈要求不要做。
summary.en: Needn’t means there is no necessity; mustn’t expresses prohibition or a strong instruction not to act.

usage.zh-Hans: You needn’t print the form 表示电子版也可以；You mustn’t print the form 表示不能打印。don’t need to 和 needn’t 在许多语境里意思相近，但语法形式不同：needn’t 后接动词原形，don’t need to 后接带 to 的不定式。谈过去时，didn’t need to do 表示没有必要，是否真的做了可能要看语境；needn’t have done 通常暗示做了但其实没必要。
usage.zh-Hant: You needn’t print the form 表示電子版也可以；You mustn’t print the form 表示不能列印。don’t need to 和 needn’t 在許多語境裡意思相近，但文法形式不同：needn’t 後接動詞原形，don’t need to 後接帶 to 的不定詞。談過去時，didn’t need to do 表示沒有必要，是否真的做了可能要看語境；needn’t have done 通常暗示做了但其實沒必要。
usage.en: You needn’t print the form allows an electronic copy; you mustn’t print it forbids printing. Don’t need to and needn’t often express similar lack of necessity, but their forms differ: needn’t takes a plain verb; don’t need to takes a to-infinitive. In the past, didn’t need to do says there was no necessity and may leave the actual action open; needn’t have done usually implies the action happened unnecessarily.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要把 You mustn’t come early 当作“不必早来”；它更像“不得早来”。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要把 You mustn’t come early 當作「不必早來」；它更像「不得早來」。
pitfall.en: Do not use You mustn’t come early to mean coming early is optional; it sounds like a ban.

entries.pattern: needn’t + base verb · don’t need to + verb · mustn’t + base verb
entries.example: You needn’t bring a pen; we have spare ones.
examples: You needn’t bring a pen; we have spare ones.
Visitors mustn’t touch the exhibits.
We did not need to book in advance.
I needn’t have bought a ticket; entry was free.
entries.contrast: You needn’t wait. · You mustn’t wait.

question.zh-Hans: whether 和 if 引导间接问句时何时不能互换？
question.zh-Hant: whether 和 if 引導間接問句時何時不能互換？
question.en: When are whether and if not interchangeable?

summary.zh-Hans: 两者都能引入许多间接是非问句；明确列出两种选择或放在介词后时，whether 更稳妥。
summary.zh-Hant: 兩者都能引入許多間接是非問句；明確列出兩種選擇或放在介系詞後時，whether 更穩妥。
summary.en: Both can introduce many embedded yes–no questions. Whether is safer with explicit alternatives and after a preposition.

usage.zh-Hans: I don’t know whether/if the door is open 两者都可。whether...or not 能明确表示两种可能；whether to leave 可接不定式，而 if to leave 不可。放在介词后用 whether，如 a discussion about whether to proceed。if 还引导条件句；当句子既可能是“是否”，也可能是“如果”，可用 whether 消除歧义。间接问句内部仍用陈述语序。
usage.zh-Hant: I don’t know whether/if the door is open 兩者都可。whether...or not 能明確表示兩種可能；whether to leave 可接不定詞，而 if to leave 不可。放在介系詞後用 whether，如 a discussion about whether to proceed。if 還引導條件句；當句子既可能是「是否」，也可能是「如果」，可用 whether 消除歧義。間接問句內部仍用陳述語序。
usage.en: I don’t know whether/if the door is open allows either word. Whether...or not makes alternatives explicit. Whether can precede a to-infinitive, but if to leave cannot. After a preposition, use whether, as in a discussion about whether to proceed. If also introduces conditions; whether can remove ambiguity between “whether” and “if” meanings. Keep statement order inside the embedded question.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 We discussed about if to leave；可说 We discussed whether to leave。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 We discussed about if to leave；可說 We discussed whether to leave。
pitfall.en: Avoid We discussed about if to leave; say We discussed whether to leave.

entries.pattern: whether/if + subject + verb · whether + to-infinitive
entries.example: I asked whether the files had arrived.
examples: I asked whether the files had arrived.
We have not decided whether to move.
The debate is about whether the rule is fair.
Tell me if the room is available.
entries.contrast: I asked if she was ready. · I asked whether she was ready or not.

title.zh-Hans: must have / might have / can’t have
title.zh-Hant: must have / might have / can’t have
title.en: must have / might have / can’t have

entries.headword: must have / might have / can’t have

question.zh-Hans: 情态动词加 have done 如何表示对过去的推断？
question.zh-Hant: 情態動詞加 have done 如何表示對過去的推斷？
question.en: How do modal perfect forms express past deductions?

summary.zh-Hans: must have done 表示对过去有把握的推断；might/may have done 表示可能；can’t have done 表示认为不可能。
summary.zh-Hant: must have done 表示對過去有把握的推斷；might/may have done 表示可能；can’t have done 表示認為不可能。
summary.en: Must have done signals a strong past deduction, might/may have done a possibility, and can’t have done an inferred impossibility.

usage.zh-Hans: 这些形式谈说话人现在如何判断过去发生的事，不是直接报告亲眼所见。The lights are off; they must have left 是根据线索推断。could have done 可表示过去的可能性或未实现的能力／机会，须看语境；should have done 常表示过去本应做却没做，和推断的语气不同。否定推断通常用 can’t have done，而不是 mustn’t have done。
usage.zh-Hant: 這些形式談說話人現在如何判斷過去發生的事，不是直接報告親眼所見。The lights are off; they must have left 是根據線索推斷。could have done 可表示過去的可能性或未實現的能力／機會，須看語境；should have done 常表示過去本應做卻沒做，和推斷的語氣不同。否定推斷通常用 can’t have done，而不是 mustn’t have done。
usage.en: These forms show the speaker’s present judgement about a past event; they are not direct eyewitness reports. The lights are off; they must have left is an inference from evidence. Could have done can suggest past possibility or an unrealised opportunity, depending on context. Should have done often criticises an action not taken, rather than making the same kind of deduction. Negative deduction normally uses can’t have done, not mustn’t have done.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要把 must have left 当成过去时的“必须离开”；义务可用 had to leave。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要把 must have left 當成過去式的「必須離開」；義務可用 had to leave。
pitfall.en: Do not use must have left for the past obligation “had to leave”; it usually expresses a deduction.

entries.pattern: modal + have + past participle
entries.example: The floor is wet; it must have rained.
examples: The floor is wet; it must have rained.
She might have missed the last bus.
He can’t have read the note; it is still sealed.
We should have checked the date earlier.
entries.contrast: She had to leave. · She must have left.

question.zh-Hans: 反意疑问句怎样选助动词和代词？
question.zh-Hant: 附加問句怎樣選助動詞和代名詞？
question.en: How do question tags choose their auxiliary and pronoun?

summary.zh-Hans: 附加问句通常呼应主句的助动词与主语，并常用相反的肯否形式。
summary.zh-Hant: 附加問句通常呼應主句的助動詞與主詞，並常用相反的肯否形式。
summary.en: A question tag normally echoes the main clause’s auxiliary and subject, often with reversed polarity.

usage.zh-Hans: She is ready, isn’t she? 用 is 与 she；They have finished, haven’t they? 用 have。主句没有助动词时，附加问句常用 do/does/did：You work here, don’t you? 命令句和 Let’s... 有自己的惯用附加形式，如 will you? 和 shall we? 语调也影响功能：下降语调常期待确认，上升语调更像真正询问；标点不能完全传达这种差别。
usage.zh-Hant: She is ready, isn’t she? 用 is 與 she；They have finished, haven’t they? 用 have。主句沒有助動詞時，附加問句常用 do/does/did：You work here, don’t you? 祈使句和 Let’s... 有自己的慣用附加形式，如 will you? 和 shall we? 語調也影響功能：下降語調常期待確認，上升語調更像真正詢問；標點不能完全傳達這種差別。
usage.en: She is ready, isn’t she? repeats is and uses she; they have finished, haven’t they? repeats have. Without an auxiliary in the main clause, use do/does/did: You work here, don’t you? Imperatives and Let’s... have conventional tags such as will you? and shall we? Intonation matters too: a falling tag often seeks confirmation, while a rising one can be a genuine question. Punctuation alone does not capture this difference.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要按中文“对吗”统一写 is it；主句的人称、时态和助动词都要核对。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要依中文「對嗎」一律寫 is it；主句的人稱、時態和助動詞都要核對。
pitfall.en: Do not append is it to every statement; check person, tense and auxiliary.

entries.pattern: statement + comma + auxiliary + pronoun?
entries.example: You sent the form, didn’t you?
examples: You sent the form, didn’t you?
Mira can drive, can’t she?
They are not late, are they?
Let’s take a break, shall we?
entries.contrast: You know Sam, don’t you? · You knew Sam, didn’t you?

question.zh-Hans: as long as 表条件时比 if 多表达什么？
question.zh-Hant: as long as 表條件時比 if 多表達什麼？
question.en: What does as long as add to a condition?

summary.zh-Hans: as long as 可表示“只要”，突出某条件是允许结果发生的要求；它也可表示时间长度。
summary.zh-Hant: as long as 可表示「只要」，凸顯某條件是容許結果發生的要求；它也可表示時間長度。
summary.en: As long as can mean provided that, highlighting a required condition; it can also refer to duration.

usage.zh-Hans: You may borrow the camera as long as you return it tonight 表示归还是借用的条件。一般的 if 只提出一种可能，并不一定突出“以此为前提”的许可。表达未来条件时，条件分句通常用现在时。as long as 也可以字面指持续时间：I stayed as long as I could。判断时看主句是条件结果，还是在比较时间长短。
usage.zh-Hant: You may borrow the camera as long as you return it tonight 表示歸還是借用的條件。一般的 if 只提出一種可能，並不一定凸顯「以此為前提」的許可。表達未來條件時，條件子句通常用現在式。as long as 也可以字面指持續時間：I stayed as long as I could。判斷時看主句是條件結果，還是在比較時間長短。
usage.en: You may borrow the camera as long as you return it tonight makes returning it a condition of permission. A plain if introduces a possibility without necessarily stressing such a requirement. In future-oriented conditions, the conditional clause normally uses a present form. As long as can also literally describe duration: I stayed as long as I could. Decide whether the sentence concerns a conditional result or length of time.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要把所有 as long as 都译成“只要”；与 stayed、waited 等动词连用时可能指“尽可能久”。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要把所有 as long as 都譯成「只要」；與 stayed、waited 等動詞連用時可能指「盡可能久」。
pitfall.en: Do not treat every as long as as conditional; with stayed or waited it may describe duration.

entries.pattern: as long as + condition · as long as + duration
entries.example: You can use the room as long as you leave it tidy.
examples: You can use the room as long as you leave it tidy.
As long as the file is complete, we can submit it.
I waited as long as the office remained open.
The offer stands as long as the stock lasts.
entries.contrast: You can join if you register. · You can join as long as you register.

question.zh-Hans: 谓语动词该用单数还是复数？
question.zh-Hant: 謂語動詞該用單數還是複數？
question.en: Should the verb be singular or plural?

summary.zh-Hans: 谓语跟语法主语的单复数走，不跟附近的名词走。中文动词不变形，英语里却要选择 is/are、has/have 或动词是否加 -s。
summary.zh-Hant: 謂語跟語法主語的單複數走，不跟附近的名詞走。中文動詞不變形，英語裡卻要選擇 is/are、has/have 或動詞是否加 -s。
summary.en: The verb agrees with the grammatical subject, not with a nearby noun. Choose is or are, has or have, and whether a present verb adds -s.

usage.zh-Hans:
先找真正的主语。The list of names is long 的主语是 list，不是 names。together with、as well as、including 后面的名词通常不把单数主语改成复数。each、every、everyone 后常用单数动词。news、mathematics 这类词形虽以 -s 结尾，动词仍用单数；people 则用复数。

there is/are 在谨慎写法中跟后面的名词一致：There is a key，There are two keys。口语里 There's two keys 很常见，但不能把它当成所有文体的标准。集体名词如 team、family，美式英语常作整体用单数，英式英语在强调成员时可用复数。either/neither of 作主语时，正式文字多用单数动词。
usage.zh-Hant:
先找真正的主語。The list of names is long 的主語是 list，不是 names。together with、as well as、including 後面的名詞通常不把單數主語改成複數。each、every、everyone 後常用單數動詞。news、mathematics 這類詞形雖以 -s 結尾，動詞仍用單數；people 則用複數。

there is/are 在謹慎寫法中跟後面的名詞一致：There is a key，There are two keys。口語裡 There's two keys 很常見，但不能把它當成所有文體的標準。集體名詞如 team、family，美式英語常作整體用單數，英式英語在強調成員時可用複數。either/neither of 作主語時，正式文字多用單數動詞。
usage.en:
Find the real subject. In The list of names is long, the subject is list, not names. Nouns after together with, as well as or including do not normally make a singular subject plural. Each, every and everyone usually take a singular verb. News and mathematics take a singular verb despite the final -s; people takes a plural verb.

In careful writing, there is or there are agrees with the following noun: There is a key, There are two keys. There's two keys is common in speech, but it is not the careful written form. A collective noun such as team or family is often singular in American English when the group is one unit, and it may be plural in British English when the members matter. With either of or neither of as subject, formal writing usually prefers a singular verb.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要因为靠近动词的名词是复数就加复数动词：The box of pencils is missing，不是 are missing。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要因為靠近動詞的名詞是複數就加複數動詞：The box of pencils is missing，不是 are missing。
pitfall.en: Do not let the nearest noun decide: The box of pencils is missing, not are missing.

examples: The list of names is long.
Everyone in the two groups has a copy.
There are two letters on the desk.
The news is better than we expected.
entries.pattern: singular subject + singular verb · plural subject + plural verb
entries.example: The list of names is long.
entries.contrast: The list of names is long. · The names on the list are long.

question.zh-Hans: 两个过去的动作，什么时候用 had + 过去分词？
question.zh-Hant: 兩個過去的動作，什麼時候用 had + 過去分詞？
question.en: When do two past events need had + past participle?

summary.zh-Hans: had + 过去分词表示在另一个过去时间之前已经发生的事。它不是更正式的一般过去时。
summary.zh-Hant: had + 過去分詞表示在另一個過去時間之前已經發生的事。它不是更正式的一般過去時。
summary.en: Use had + past participle for an event before another past time. It is not a more formal past simple.

usage.zh-Hans:
先确定两个过去时间谁更早。When we arrived, the talk had started 里，开始早于到达。already、just、never 常帮助标出这个更早的过去。如果 before 或 after 已经把顺序说清，两个一般过去时往往就够：I locked the door before I left。过去完成时在顺序否则会含糊时尤其有用。

不要把所有“过去的过去”都套成 had。单独叙述一串按时间推进的事件，通常用一般过去时。过去完成时的时间参照是另一个过去点，不是现在；跟现在有关的“已经”仍用现在完成时。
usage.zh-Hant:
先確定兩個過去時間誰更早。When we arrived, the talk had started 裡，開始早於到達。already、just、never 常幫助標出這個更早的過去。如果 before 或 after 已經把順序說清，兩個一般過去時往往就夠：I locked the door before I left。過去完成時在順序否則會含糊時尤其有用。

不要把所有“過去的過去”都套成 had。單獨敘述一串按時間推進的事件，通常用一般過去時。過去完成時的時間參照是另一個過去點，不是現在；跟現在有關的“已經”仍用現在完成時。
usage.en:
Decide which of two past times is earlier. In When we arrived, the talk had started, the start is earlier than the arrival. Already, just and never often mark that earlier past. If before or after already makes the order clear, two past-simple verbs are often enough: I locked the door before I left. The past perfect is most useful when the order would otherwise be unclear.

Do not put had on every past event. A sequence told in time order normally uses the past simple. The past perfect takes another past moment as its reference, not now; a past event linked to the present still uses the present perfect.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要把较晚的那个过去动作写成 had：到达是后发生的，所以不是 When we had arrived, the talk started，除非你另有更晚的参照点。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要把較晚的那個過去動作寫成 had：到達是後發生的，所以不是 When we had arrived, the talk started，除非你另有更晚的參照點。
pitfall.en: Do not mark the later past event with had. The arrival is later, so When we had arrived, the talk started reverses the usual timeline unless another later point is intended.

examples: When we arrived, the talk had already started.
She had left before I reached the office.
I locked the door before I left.
By noon, the parcel had arrived.
entries.pattern: had + past participle, before a later past
entries.example: When we arrived, the talk had already started.
entries.contrast: The talk started, and then we arrived. · When we arrived, the talk had started.

question.zh-Hans: had been doing 和 was doing 有什么不同？
question.zh-Hant: had been doing 和 was doing 有什麼不同？
question.en: How is had been doing different from was doing?

summary.zh-Hans: had been + -ing 表示一个活动一直持续到某个过去时刻，常说明那时的结果。was doing 表示那个时刻正在进行。
summary.zh-Hant: had been + -ing 表示一個活動一直持續到某個過去時刻，常說明那時的結果。was doing 表示那個時刻正在進行。
summary.en: Had been + -ing shows an activity continuing up to a past moment, often with a result then. Was doing means in progress at that moment.

usage.zh-Hans:
用过去完成进行时回答“到那个过去点之前，这个活动进行了多久或重复了多久”。I had been waiting for an hour when the bus came。结果也常一起出现：她眼睛红，是因为她之前一直在改稿。状态动词如 know、own 通常不用进行体。

was waiting 的镜头停在那个时刻内部；had been waiting 的镜头从更早拉到那个时刻。如果只是说当时正在等，没有“此前一直”的意思，用过去进行时即可。
usage.zh-Hant:
用過去完成進行時回答“到那個過去點之前，這個活動進行了多久或重複了多久”。I had been waiting for an hour when the bus came。結果也常一起出現：她眼睛紅，是因為她之前一直在改稿。狀態動詞如 know、own 通常不用進行體。

was waiting 的鏡頭停在那個時刻內部；had been waiting 的鏡頭從更早拉到那個時刻。如果只是說當時正在等，沒有“此前一直”的意思，用過去進行時即可。
usage.en:
Use the past perfect continuous to say how long, or how repeatedly, an activity had been going on before a past point. I had been waiting for an hour when the bus came. A result is often visible too: her eyes were red because she had been editing. Stative verbs such as know or own do not normally take this form.

Was waiting places the camera inside that moment. Had been waiting runs from an earlier time up to that moment. If you only mean that the waiting was in progress then, the past continuous is enough.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要把“当时正在做”写成 had been doing。The phone rang while I was cooking 并不需要 had been。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要把“當時正在做”寫成 had been doing。The phone rang while I was cooking 並不需要 had been。
pitfall.en: Do not use had been doing for an action simply in progress then. The phone rang while I was cooking does not need had been.

examples: I had been waiting for an hour when the bus came.
Her eyes were red because she had been editing.
The phone rang while I was cooking.
They had been living there for years before the move.
entries.pattern: had been + -ing, up to a past point
entries.example: I had been waiting for an hour when the bus came.
entries.contrast: I was waiting when the bus came. · I had been waiting for an hour when it came.

question.zh-Hans: 什么时候说 will be doing？
question.zh-Hant: 什麼時候說 will be doing？
question.en: When is will be doing the right future?

summary.zh-Hans: will be + -ing 表示将来某个时刻正在进行的事，也可用来礼貌地询问对方计划。临时决定不用这个形式。
summary.zh-Hant: will be + -ing 表示將來某個時刻正在進行的事，也可用來禮貌地詢問對方計劃。臨時決定不用這個形式。
summary.en: Will be + -ing marks an action in progress at a future time, and it can politely ask about someone's plans. A sudden decision uses a different future.

usage.zh-Hans:
把时间点说清：At 8 tomorrow I will be sitting on the train。这个形式常表示事情会自然地处于进行中，而不是说话人此刻刚决定去做。礼貌问句 Will you be passing the post office? 把对方的行程当作已有安排来问，比 Will you pass...? 少一些“请你去做”的压力。

临时决定、承诺或对一次完整动作的预测，通常用 will + 原形：I'll open the window。安排好的私人日程更常用现在进行时：I'm meeting Sam at 8。将来进行时的助动词是 will be，后面必须是 -ing。
usage.zh-Hant:
把時間點說清：At 8 tomorrow I will be sitting on the train。這個形式常表示事情會自然地處於進行中，而不是說話人此刻剛決定去做。禮貌問句 Will you be passing the post office? 把對方的行程當作已有安排來問，比 Will you pass...? 少一些“請你去做”的壓力。

臨時決定、承諾或對一次完整動作的預測，通常用 will + 原形：I'll open the window。安排好的私人日程更常用現在進行時：I'm meeting Sam at 8。將來進行時的助動詞是 will be，後面必須是 -ing。
usage.en:
Name the future point: At 8 tomorrow I will be sitting on the train. This form often presents the action as in progress as a matter of course, not as a decision made at the moment of speaking. Will you be passing the post office? treats the route as an existing plan and is less pressing than Will you pass...?

A sudden decision, promise or prediction of a complete action normally uses will + base form: I'll open the window. A fixed personal arrangement more often uses the present continuous: I'm meeting Sam at 8. The pattern is will be plus an -ing form.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要漏掉 -ing，也不要在 will be 后面用过去分词：At 8 I will be travelling，不是 will be travel，也不是 will be travelled。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要漏掉 -ing，也不要在 will be 後面用過去分詞：At 8 I will be travelling，不是 will be travel，也不是 will be travelled。
pitfall.en: Do not drop the -ing, and do not use a past participle: At 8 I will be travelling, not will be travel or will be travelled.

examples: At 8 tomorrow I will be sitting on the train.
Will you be passing the post office?
This time next week we will be moving house.
I'll open the window.
entries.pattern: will be + -ing at a future time
entries.example: At 8 tomorrow I will be sitting on the train.
entries.contrast: I'll open the window. · At 8 I will be sitting on the train.

question.zh-Hans: 怎样说将来某个时刻之前会已经完成？
question.zh-Hant: 怎樣說將來某個時刻之前會已經完成？
question.en: How do I say something will be finished before a future time?

summary.zh-Hans: will have + 过去分词表示在将来的截止点之前完成。by、by the time 常和它一起出现。
summary.zh-Hant: will have + 過去分詞表示在將來的截止點之前完成。by、by the time 常和它一起出現。
summary.en: Will have + past participle means completed before a future deadline. By and by the time often supply that deadline.

usage.zh-Hans:
先找截止点，再决定动作是否在那之前完成。By June she will have finished the course 的意思不是“六月正在做完”，而是“到六月时，完成已经成为事实”。by the time 引导的时间从句用现在时，主句用将来完成时：By the time you arrive, I will have left。

如果只是说将来会做，没有“在那之前已经完成”，用 will + 原形或 be going to。将来完成时不把 have 后面的动词留在原形。
usage.zh-Hant:
先找截止點，再決定動作是否在那之前完成。By June she will have finished the course 的意思不是“六月正在做完”，而是“到六月時，完成已經成為事實”。by the time 引導的時間從句用現在時，主句用將來完成時：By the time you arrive, I will have left。

如果只是說將來會做，沒有“在那之前已經完成”，用 will + 原形或 be going to。將來完成時不把 have 後面的動詞留在原形。
usage.en:
Find the deadline first, then decide whether the action is complete before it. By June she will have finished the course means that completion is already a fact at June, not that the finishing happens during June. A by the time clause uses a present form, and the main clause uses the future perfect: By the time you arrive, I will have left.

If you only mean that something will happen, without completion before a point, use will + base form or be going to. Do not leave the verb after have in the base form.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 will have finish，也不要在 by the time 从句里加 will：By the time you arrive, I will have left。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 will have finish，也不要在 by the time 從句里加 will：By the time you arrive, I will have left。
pitfall.en: Avoid will have finish, and do not put will in the by the time clause: By the time you arrive, I will have left.

examples: By June she will have finished the course.
By the time you arrive, I will have left.
The paint will have dried before we move the desk.
She will finish the course next year.
entries.pattern: will have + past participle by a future point
entries.example: By June she will have finished the course.
entries.contrast: She will finish in June. · By June she will have finished.

question.zh-Hans: 谈将来时，什么时候不用 will？
question.zh-Hant: 談將來時，什麼時候不用 will？
question.en: When does a future meaning not use will?

summary.zh-Hans: 时刻表和节目常用一般现在时；已经安排好的私人日程常用现在进行时。will 更适合决定、承诺和预测。
summary.zh-Hant: 時刻表和節目常用一般現在時；已經安排好的私人日程常用現在進行時。will 更適合決定、承諾和預測。
summary.en: Timetables and programmes often use the present simple. A fixed personal arrangement often uses the present continuous. Will fits decisions, promises and predictions.

usage.zh-Hans:
火车、航班、课程、演出按时间表运行时，常用一般现在时：The train leaves at 6。这不是说事情现在发生，而是把将来当作既定日程。自己已经约好的事，常用现在进行时：I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow。说话时才决定或只是预测，用 will 或 be going to。

时间从句和 if 从句里谈将来，也常用现在时，不用 will：I'll call you when I land。中文可以在各种将来意思上用“会”，英语却要先看是时刻表、安排、决定还是从句。
usage.zh-Hant:
火車、航班、課程、演出按時間表運行時，常用一般現在時：The train leaves at 6。這不是說事情現在發生，而是把將來當作既定日程。自己已經約好的事，常用現在進行時：I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow。說話時才決定或只是預測，用 will 或 be going to。

時間從句和 if 從句裡談將來，也常用現在時，不用 will：I'll call you when I land。中文可以在各種將來意思上用“會”，英語卻要先看是時刻表、安排、決定還是從句。
usage.en:
When a train, flight, class or performance runs to a timetable, the present simple is normal: The train leaves at 6. That does not mean it is happening now; it treats the future as a fixed schedule. For something you have already arranged, the present continuous is usual: I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow. A decision made while speaking, or a prediction, uses will or be going to.

Future time clauses and if-clauses also use a present form, not will: I'll call you when I land. One future word in Chinese does not map onto every English future. First ask whether you mean a timetable, an arrangement, a decision or a subordinate clause.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要把所有将来都写成 will。The train leaves at 6 是时刻表；I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow 是已安排的事。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要把所有將來都寫成 will。The train leaves at 6 是時刻表；I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow 是已安排的事。
pitfall.en: Do not put will on every future. The train leaves at 6 is a timetable; I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow is an arrangement.

examples: The train leaves at 6.
I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow.
I'll call you when I land.
I think it will rain later.
entries.pattern: present simple for timetables · present continuous for arrangements
entries.example: The train leaves at 6.
entries.contrast: The train leaves at 6. · I'll get a later train.

question.zh-Hans: 为什么有些动词通常不用进行时？
question.zh-Hant: 為什麼有些動詞通常不用進行時？
question.en: Why do some verbs avoid the continuous?

summary.zh-Hans: 表示知道、喜欢、拥有、感觉或看起来怎样的动词，通常用简单时态。同一动词若表示活动，就可以用进行时。
summary.zh-Hant: 表示知道、喜歡、擁有、感覺或看起來怎樣的動詞，通常用簡單時態。同一動詞若表示活動，就可以用進行時。
summary.en: Verbs of knowing, liking, owning, sensing or seeming usually take simple forms. The same verb can take a continuous form when it means an activity.

usage.zh-Hans:
know、believe、like、own、seem、belong 描写的是状态，不是正在一步步做的动作，所以 I know her 不用 I'm knowing her。中文“在”不能自动翻译成英语进行时。have 表示拥有时用简单时态：I have a car；表示活动时可以：I'm having lunch。think 表示看法用 I think；表示正在考虑用 I'm thinking。

see、hear、smell、taste 在“无意识地感知”时常用简单时态，或用 can see、can hear。若是约见、观看、主动闻或尝，进行时就自然：I'm seeing the dentist，I'm tasting the soup。先问这个词在句中是状态还是活动。
usage.zh-Hant:
know、believe、like、own、seem、belong 描寫的是狀態，不是正在一步步做的動作，所以 I know her 不用 I'm knowing her。中文“在”不能自動翻譯成英語進行時。have 表示擁有時用簡單時態：I have a car；表示活動時可以：I'm having lunch。think 表示看法用 I think；表示正在考慮用 I'm thinking。

see、hear、smell、taste 在“無意識地感知”時常用簡單時態，或用 can see、can hear。若是約見、觀看、主動聞或嘗，進行時就自然：I'm seeing the dentist，I'm tasting the soup。先問這個詞在句中是狀態還是活動。
usage.en:
Know, believe, like, own, seem and belong describe states rather than step-by-step actions, so say I know her, not I'm knowing her. A progressive marker in Chinese does not automatically become an English continuous form. Have for possession stays simple: I have a car. Have for an activity can be continuous: I'm having lunch. I think gives an opinion; I'm thinking means the considering is in progress.

See, hear, smell and taste usually stay simple, or use can, for involuntary perception. When they mean a meeting, watching, or deliberate smelling or tasting, the continuous is natural: I'm seeing the dentist, I'm tasting the soup. Ask whether the verb is a state or an activity in that sentence.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 I'm knowing、I'm owning 或 I'm having a car。拥有用 I have a car；吃饭才说 I'm having lunch。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 I'm knowing、I'm owning 或 I'm having a car。擁有用 I have a car；吃飯才說 I'm having lunch。
pitfall.en: Avoid I'm knowing, I'm owning and I'm having a car. Possession is I have a car; a meal can be I'm having lunch.

examples: I know her, but I don't know her address.
I'm having lunch with the editor.
I think it's ready. I'm thinking about the title.
I can hear a train.
entries.pattern: simple form for a state · continuous form for an activity
entries.example: I know her, but I don't know her address.
entries.contrast: I have a car. · I'm having lunch.

question.zh-Hans: always、often、never 放在动词的哪一边？
question.zh-Hant: always、often、never 放在動詞的哪一邊？
question.en: Where do always, often and never go?

summary.zh-Hans: always、usually、often、sometimes、rarely、never 通常放在主要动词前；如果有 be，就放在 be 后面。
summary.zh-Hant: always、usually、often、sometimes、rarely、never 通常放在主要動詞前；如果有 be，就放在 be 後面。
summary.en: Always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely and never normally go before the main verb, or after be.

usage.zh-Hans:
She always arrives early 里，always 在 arrives 前。She is always early 里，always 在 is 后。有助动词时，放在第一个助动词后：I have never tried it。sometimes 和 often 也可以放在句末：I walk to work sometimes。

never、rarely、seldom 已经含有否定意思，不要再加 not。句首的 Always she is early 只在强调时偶尔出现，不是普通位置。频度副词回答“多久一次”，不回答“怎样做”。
usage.zh-Hant:
She always arrives early 裡，always 在 arrives 前。She is always early 裡，always 在 is 後。有助動詞時，放在第一個助動詞後：I have never tried it。sometimes 和 often 也可以放在句末：I walk to work sometimes。

never、rarely、seldom 已經含有否定意思，不要再加 not。句首的 Always she is early 只在強調時偶爾出現，不是普通位置。頻度副詞回答“多久一次”，不回答“怎樣做”。
usage.en:
In She always arrives early, always comes before arrives. In She is always early, it comes after is. With an auxiliary, it follows the first auxiliary: I have never tried it. Sometimes and often can also end the sentence: I walk to work sometimes.

Never, rarely and seldom are already negative, so do not add not. Always she is early is an occasional emphasis, not the ordinary position. These adverbs answer how often, not how.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要把 always 一律放在句首，也不要写 She doesn't never arrive。never 本身就是否定。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要把 always 一律放在句首，也不要寫 She doesn't never arrive。never 本身就是否定。
pitfall.en: Do not put always at the start by default, and avoid She doesn't never arrive. Never is already negative.

examples: She always arrives early.
She is always early.
I have never tried this route.
I walk to work sometimes.
entries.pattern: before the main verb · after be
entries.example: She always arrives early.
entries.contrast: She always arrives early. · She is always early.

title.en: can, could and be able to

question.zh-Hans: 能力用 can、could 还是 be able to？
question.zh-Hant: 能力用 can、could 還是 be able to？
question.en: Can, could, or be able to for ability?

summary.zh-Hans: can 表示现在的能力、可能或非正式许可。could 表示过去的一般能力、较委婉的请求或现在的可能性。某一次过去做成了，常用 was able to。
summary.zh-Hant: can 表示現在的能力、可能或非正式許可。could 表示過去的一般能力、較委婉的請求或現在的可能性。某一次過去做成了，常用 was able to。
summary.en: Can is for present ability, possibility or informal permission. Could is for general past ability, a polite request or present possibility. A specific past success is often was able to.

usage.zh-Hans:
I can swim 是现在的能力。I could swim when I was five 是过去长期具备的能力。若强调过去某一具体场合终于做成，英语常用 was/were able to 或 managed to：The exit was blocked, but we were able to climb out。这个场合若没做成，couldn't 和 wasn't able to 都可以。

can 没有不定式，所以其他时态要用 be able to：I will be able to help tomorrow，She has been able to walk again。could 也可以表示现在较小的把握：That could be the reason。中文“能、会、可以”都可能对应 can，但许可、能力和可能性并不相同。
usage.zh-Hant:
I can swim 是現在的能力。I could swim when I was five 是過去長期具備的能力。若強調過去某一具體場合終於做成，英語常用 was/were able to 或 managed to：The exit was blocked, but we were able to climb out。這個場合若沒做成，couldn't 和 wasn't able to 都可以。

can 沒有不定式，所以其他時態要用 be able to：I will be able to help tomorrow，She has been able to walk again。could 也可以表示現在較小的把握：That could be the reason。中文“能、會、可以”都可能對應 can，但許可、能力和可能性並不相同。
usage.en:
I can swim is present ability. I could swim when I was five is a general ability in the past. For one past occasion when someone succeeded, English often uses was/were able to or managed to: The exit was blocked, but we were able to climb out. If the attempt failed, both couldn't and wasn't able to are fine.

Can has no infinitive, so other tenses use be able to: I will be able to help tomorrow, She has been able to walk again. Could can also give a present possibility with less certainty: That could be the reason. The Chinese words for ability and permission do not all map to one English modal.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要用 I could climb out 来强调过去某一次终于逃脱；这种具体成功常用 we were able to climb out。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要用 I could climb out 來強調過去某一次終於逃脫；這種具體成功常用 we were able to climb out。
pitfall.en: Do not rely on I could climb out for one past success. That specific success is normally we were able to climb out.

examples: I can swim, but I can't dive.
I could swim when I was five.
The exit was blocked, but we were able to climb out.
I will be able to help tomorrow.
entries.pattern: can for now · could for general past ability · was able to for one success
entries.example: I can swim, but I can't dive.
entries.contrast: I could swim as a child. · We were able to climb out.

title.en: should, ought to and had better

question.zh-Hans: 建议用 should、ought to 还是 had better？
question.zh-Hant: 建議用 should、ought to 還是 had better？
question.en: Should, ought to, or had better for advice?

summary.zh-Hans: should 和 ought to 都表示建议或预期。had better 针对眼前情况，暗示不这么做会有不好的结果。
summary.zh-Hant: should 和 ought to 都表示建議或預期。had better 針對眼前情況，暗示不這麼做會有不好的結果。
summary.en: Should and ought to give advice or an expectation. Had better is for a particular situation and hints at a bad result if you do not act.

usage.zh-Hans:
You should save a copy 是普通建议。ought to 意思接近，语气稍正式，口语里少一些；否定是 ought not to，但实际常用 shouldn't。should 还可以表示预期：The train should be here soon。

had better 里的 had 不表示过去。You had better leave now 谈的是现在或将来，常缩成 You'd better leave now。后面用原形，不加 to；否定是 had better not。它比 should 更像针对这一次的警告。不应把它写成 would better。
usage.zh-Hant:
You should save a copy 是普通建議。ought to 意思接近，語氣稍正式，口語裡少一些；否定是 ought not to，但實際常用 shouldn't。should 還可以表示預期：The train should be here soon。

had better 裡的 had 不表示過去。You had better leave now 談的是現在或將來，常縮成 You'd better leave now。後面用原形，不加 to；否定是 had better not。它比 should 更像針對這一次的警告。不應把它寫成 would better。
usage.en:
You should save a copy is ordinary advice. Ought to is close in meaning and a little more formal, and it is less common in speech. The negative is ought not to, though shouldn't is more usual. Should can also mark expectation: The train should be here soon.

The had in had better is not a past tense. You had better leave now is about the present or future, often shortened to You'd better leave now. Use the base form, with no to. The negative is had better not. It is a warning for this situation rather than a general recommendation. Do not turn it into would better.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要在 had better 后加 to，也不要写成 would better：You'd better leave，不是 You'd better to leave。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要在 had better 後加 to，也不要寫成 would better：You'd better leave，不是 You'd better to leave。
pitfall.en: Do not add to after had better, and do not write would better: You'd better leave, not You'd better to leave.

examples: You should save a copy.
The train should be here soon.
You'd better leave now.
You'd better not park in front of the gate.
entries.pattern: should + verb · ought to + verb · had better + verb
entries.example: You should save a copy.
entries.contrast: You should save a copy. · You'd better leave now.

question.zh-Hans: may 和 might 都是“可能”吗？
question.zh-Hant: may 和 might 都是“可能”嗎？
question.en: Do may and might both mean possibility?

summary.zh-Hans: may 和 might 都可表示可能；might 常常把握更小，但不是 may 的过去式专属形式。may 还可表示正式许可。
summary.zh-Hant: may 和 might 都可表示可能；might 常常把握更小，但不是 may 的過去式專屬形式。may 還可表示正式許可。
summary.en: May and might both mark possibility. Might often sounds less certain, but it is not only the past of may. May can also give formal permission.

usage.zh-Hans:
It may rain 和 It might rain 都表示下雨有可能，might 常让把握听起来更低，不过实际差别不一定很大。may 表示许可时比较正式：You may leave when you have signed。口语许可更常用 can。might 在间接引语里常对应原来的 may：She said it might rain。

二者后面都用原形，不加 to。对过去可能性要用 may have 或 might have + 过去分词。maybe 是副词，不能替换句中的 may be。否定 may not 既可以是“不准”，也可以是“可能不”，要看语境；cannot 则常表示能力不足或较明确的不允许。
usage.zh-Hant:
It may rain 和 It might rain 都表示下雨有可能，might 常讓把握聽起來更低，不過實際差別不一定很大。may 表示許可時比較正式：You may leave when you have signed。口語許可更常用 can。might 在間接引語裡常對應原來的 may：She said it might rain。

二者後面都用原形，不加 to。對過去可能性要用 may have 或 might have + 過去分詞。maybe 是副詞，不能替換句中的 may be。否定 may not 既可以是“不準”，也可以是“可能不”，要看語境；cannot 則常表示能力不足或較明確的不允許。
usage.en:
It may rain and It might rain both mean rain is possible. Might often sounds less certain, though the difference is not fixed. May for permission is formal: You may leave when you have signed. Everyday permission is more often can. In reported speech, might often replaces an original may: She said it might rain.

Both take the base form, with no to. Past possibility uses may have or might have plus a past participle. Maybe is an adverb and cannot replace may be. May not can be a refusal or a possibility, depending on context; cannot more often marks inability or a clearer prohibition.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 may to go。可能是 It may rain；副词是 Maybe it will rain。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 may to go。可能是 It may rain；副詞是 Maybe it will rain。
pitfall.en: Do not write may to go. Possibility is It may rain; the adverb is Maybe it will rain.

examples: It may rain this afternoon.
It might rain, so take a coat.
You may leave when you have signed.
She said it might rain.
entries.pattern: may / might + base verb
entries.example: It may rain this afternoon.
entries.contrast: You may leave now. · It might rain.

question.zh-Hans: would 是过去、习惯，还是客气说法？
question.zh-Hant: would 是過去、習慣，還是客氣說法？
question.en: Is would past, habit, or politeness?

summary.zh-Hans: would 可以是条件结果、委婉请求、过去的重复习惯，或从过去看将来。它通常不表示某一次已经完成的过去动作。
summary.zh-Hant: would 可以是條件結果、委婉請求、過去的重複習慣，或從過去看將來。它通常不表示某一次已經完成的過去動作。
summary.en: Would can be a conditional result, a polite request, a repeated past habit, or a future seen from the past. It does not normally report one completed past event.

usage.zh-Hans:
条件句里，would 常在结果分句：If I had time, I would walk。请求和提供用 Would you...?、Would you like...?，比 will 更委婉。过去反复发生的动作也可以用 would：Every summer we would visit my aunt。状态或过去曾经存在的情况要用 used to：I used to be shy，不是 I would be shy。

从过去看后来的事，will 常变成 would：I knew she would be late。不要用 would 加明确的过去时间来叙述一次完成的事：I would see him yesterday 不正确，应说 I saw him yesterday。
usage.zh-Hant:
條件句裡，would 常在結果分句：If I had time, I would walk。請求和提供用 Would you...?、Would you like...?，比 will 更委婉。過去反覆發生的動作也可以用 would：Every summer we would visit my aunt。狀態或過去曾經存在的情況要用 used to：I used to be shy，不是 I would be shy。

從過去看後來的事，will 常變成 would：I knew she would be late。不要用 would 加明確的過去時間來敘述一次完成的事：I would see him yesterday 不正確，應說 I saw him yesterday。
usage.en:
In conditions, would usually sits in the result: If I had time, I would walk. Requests and offers use Would you...? and Would you like...?, which are softer than will. A repeated past action can also use would: Every summer we would visit my aunt. A past state uses used to: I used to be shy, not I would be shy.

Seen from the past, will often becomes would: I knew she would be late. Do not use would plus a finished past time for one completed event. I would see him yesterday is not English; say I saw him yesterday.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要用 would 表示过去的状态。I used to live there 可以；I would live there 听起来像反复的习惯或条件结果。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要用 would 表示過去的狀態。I used to live there 可以；I would live there 聽起來像反覆的習慣或條件結果。
pitfall.en: Do not use would for a past state. I used to live there is the state; I would live there sounds like a repeated habit or a conditional result.

examples: If I had time, I would walk.
Would you like a seat?
Every summer we would visit my aunt.
I knew she would be late.
entries.pattern: would + base verb
entries.example: If I had time, I would walk.
entries.contrast: Every summer we would visit my aunt. · I used to be shy.

question.zh-Hans: 什么时候用 myself、himself 而不是 me、him？
question.zh-Hant: 什麼時候用 myself、himself 而不是 me、him？
question.en: When do I use myself or himself instead of me or him?

summary.zh-Hans: 主语和宾语是同一个人时用反身代词。反身代词也可用来强调“本人”。两人互相做某事用 each other。
summary.zh-Hant: 主語和賓語是同一個人時用反身代詞。反身代詞也可用來強調“本人”。兩人互相做某事用 each other。
summary.en: Use a reflexive when the subject and object are the same person. A reflexive can also emphasise the person. Two people acting on each other need each other.

usage.zh-Hans:
He cut himself 里，割伤的人和被割伤的人相同。强调用反身代词时，句子即使去掉它仍然成立：I fixed the lock myself。by myself 可以表示独自一人，也可以表示没有别人帮忙。you 的单数是 yourself，复数是 yourselves。标准形式是 himself、themselves，不是 hisself、theirselves。

两人互相看见，用 They saw each other，不是 They saw themselves。衣服和身体部位常用物主代词：He put his hand in his pocket。反身代词不作普通主语：不要写 Myself will do it。
usage.zh-Hant:
He cut himself 裡，割傷的人和被割傷的人相同。強調用反身代詞時，句子即使去掉它仍然成立：I fixed the lock myself。by myself 可以表示獨自一人，也可以表示沒有別人幫忙。you 的單數是 yourself，複數是 yourselves。標準形式是 himself、themselves，不是 hisself、theirselves。

兩人互相看見，用 They saw each other，不是 They saw themselves。衣服和身體部位常用物主代詞：He put his hand in his pocket。反身代詞不作普通主語：不要寫 Myself will do it。
usage.en:
In He cut himself, the person who cuts and the person cut are the same. For emphasis, the sentence still works if you remove the pronoun: I fixed the lock myself. By myself can mean alone or without help. Singular you uses yourself; plural you uses yourselves. The standard forms are himself and themselves, not hisself or theirselves.

When two people see one another, say They saw each other, not They saw themselves. Clothes and body parts normally take a possessive: He put his hand in his pocket. A reflexive is not an ordinary subject: avoid Myself will do it.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 theirselves 或 hisself，也不要把互相的动作写成 themselves：They saw each other。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 theirselves 或 hisself，也不要把互相的動作寫成 themselves：They saw each other。
pitfall.en: Do not write theirselves or hisself, and do not use themselves for a mutual action: They saw each other.

examples: He cut himself while opening the tin.
I fixed the lock myself.
They saw each other at the station.
She went to the talk by herself.
entries.pattern: subject + verb + reflexive · by + reflexive
entries.example: He cut himself while opening the tin.
entries.contrast: He cut himself. · They saw each other.

question.zh-Hans: this 和 that 怎么选，后面名词要不要变复数？
question.zh-Hant: this 和 that 怎麼選，後面名詞要不要變複數？
question.en: How do I choose this or that, and when is the noun plural?

summary.zh-Hans: this/these 多指较近、当前或即将说到的事物；that/those 多指较远或刚刚说过的事物。this/that 接单数，these/those 接复数。
summary.zh-Hant: this/these 多指較近、當前或即將說到的事物；that/those 多指較遠或剛剛說過的事物。this/that 接單數，these/those 接複數。
summary.en: This and these often mark what is near, current or about to be mentioned. That and those often mark what is farther away or just mentioned. This and that take singular nouns; these and those take plurals.

usage.zh-Hans:
空间上，this cup 是手边的杯子，that cup 是远处的杯子。时间或语篇上，this 可以预告下文：This is the plan。that 可以回指刚说过的话：That is exactly the problem。电话里介绍自己常用 This is Mina。

指示词和名词要一致：this book、these books，不是 this books。kind、sort、type 在谨慎写法中用 that kind of problem，不用 those kind of problem。没有名词时，this/that 也可以单独作主语。
usage.zh-Hant:
空間上，this cup 是手邊的杯子，that cup 是遠處的杯子。時間或語篇上，this 可以預告下文：This is the plan。that 可以回指剛說過的話：That is exactly the problem。電話裡介紹自己常用 This is Mina。

指示詞和名詞要一致：this book、these books，不是 this books。kind、sort、type 在謹慎寫法中用 that kind of problem，不用 those kind of problem。沒有名詞時，this/that 也可以單獨作主語。
usage.en:
In space, this cup is the one at hand and that cup is farther away. In time or in a text, this can point forward: This is the plan. That can point back: That is exactly the problem. On the phone, This is Mina introduces the speaker.

Match the number: this book, these books, not this books. In careful writing, kind, sort and type stay singular in that kind of problem, not those kind of problem. This and that can also stand alone as subjects.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 this books 或 those kind of problem。单数用 this/that，复数用 these/those。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 this books 或 those kind of problem。單數用 this/that，複數用 these/those。
pitfall.en: Avoid this books and those kind of problem. Use this or that with a singular noun and these or those with a plural.

examples: This cup is clean, but that one is not.
These boxes go upstairs.
This is Mina speaking.
That is exactly the problem.
entries.pattern: this / that + singular · these / those + plural
entries.example: This cup is clean, but that one is not.
entries.contrast: This cup is mine. · Those cups are yours.

question.zh-Hans: whose 和 who's 怎样区分？
question.zh-Hant: whose 和 who's 怎樣區分？
question.en: Which is whose, and which is who's?

summary.zh-Hans: whose 表示“谁的”，用于疑问句和关系从句。who's 是 who is 或 who has 的缩写。
summary.zh-Hant: whose 表示“誰的”，用於疑問句和關係從句。who's 是 who is 或 who has 的縮寫。
summary.en: Whose means belonging to whom, in questions and relative clauses. Who's is the short form of who is or who has.

usage.zh-Hans:
Whose bag is this? 问的是所有者。关系从句里，whose 连接人和所属的事物：the student whose bag is missing。who's late 等于 who is late；who's finished 等于 who has finished。读音相同，只能靠句子里有没有所有关系来判断。

中文“的”不一定都写成 whose。普通物主用 her、their：the student and her bag。只有“谁的”或关系从句里的所属才用 whose。不要把 who's 的撇号省掉后当成所有格。
usage.zh-Hant:
Whose bag is this? 問的是所有者。關係從句裡，whose 連接人和所屬的事物：the student whose bag is missing。who's late 等於 who is late；who's finished 等於 who has finished。讀音相同，只能靠句子裡有沒有所有關係來判斷。

中文“的”不一定都寫成 whose。普通物主用 her、their：the student and her bag。只有“誰的”或關係從句裡的所屬才用 whose。不要把 who's 的撇號省掉後當成所有格。
usage.en:
Whose bag is this? asks for the owner. In a relative clause, whose links a person to something belonging to them: the student whose bag is missing. Who's late means who is late; who's finished means who has finished. The words sound the same, so the test is whether the sentence needs possession.

Not every possessive in Chinese becomes whose. An ordinary possessive is her or their: the student and her bag. Use whose for the question whose or for possession inside a relative clause. Leaving the apostrophe out of who's does not make a possessive.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 the student who's bag is missing。所属是 whose bag；who's bag 会变成 who is bag。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 the student who's bag is missing。所屬是 whose bag；who's bag 會變成 who is bag。
pitfall.en: Do not write the student who's bag is missing. Possession is whose bag; who's bag would mean who is bag.

examples: Whose bag is this?
The student whose bag is missing is at the desk.
Who's late this morning?
Who's finished the first page?
entries.pattern: whose + noun · who's = who is / who has
entries.example: Whose bag is this?
entries.contrast: Whose bag is this? · Who's late?

title.en: at, in and on for place

question.zh-Hans: 地点用 at、in 还是 on？
question.zh-Hant: 地點用 at、in 還是 on？
question.en: At, in, or on for a place?

summary.zh-Hans: at 多用于点、活动或门口这类位置；in 多用于范围或封闭空间；on 多用于表面、线路或登上公共交通。
summary.zh-Hant: at 多用於點、活動或門口這類位置；in 多用於範圍或封閉空間；on 多用於表面、線路或登上公共交通。
summary.en: At often marks a point, event or doorway. In often marks an area or enclosed space. On often marks a surface, a line or being aboard public transport.

usage.zh-Hans:
中文“在”覆盖了 at、in、on。可以先想位置是一个点、一个空间，还是一个表面。at the door、at the station 把地方看成到达或活动的点；in the room、in China 把地方看成在其中；on the wall、on the coast 是在表面上或沿线。公共交通常用 on the bus、on the train、on the plane；小汽车里常用 in the car。

有些搭配是固定的：at home、at work、in bed、in the picture。城市和国家一般用 in；具体地址或某个点可以用 at。街道用 live on a street 或 live in a street 都有人说，重要的是先掌握点、空间、表面这三组，再记例外。
usage.zh-Hant:
中文“在”覆蓋了 at、in、on。可以先想位置是一個點、一個空間，還是一個表面。at the door、at the station 把地方看成到達或活動的點；in the room、in China 把地方看成在其中；on the wall、on the coast 是在表面上或沿線。公共交通常用 on the bus、on the train、on the plane；小汽車裡常用 in the car。

有些搭配是固定的：at home、at work、in bed、in the picture。城市和國家一般用 in；具體地址或某個點可以用 at。街道用 live on a street 或 live in a street 都有人說，重要的是先掌握點、空間、表面這三組，再記例外。
usage.en:
One place word in Chinese covers at, in and on. Ask whether the place is a point, a space or a surface. At the door and at the station treat the place as a point of arrival or activity. In the room and in China treat it as a space you are inside. On the wall and on the coast are a surface or a line. Public transport normally uses on the bus, on the train and on the plane; a private car normally uses in the car.

Some combinations are fixed: at home, at work, in bed, in the picture. Cities and countries normally take in; a specific address or point can take at. Both live on a street and live in a street occur. Learn the point, space and surface groups before the exceptions.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要把所有“在”都写成 in。在门口是 at the door，在墙上是 on the wall，在房间里才是 in the room。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要把所有“在”都寫成 in。在門口是 at the door，在牆上是 on the wall，在房間裡才是 in the room。
pitfall.en: Do not translate every place as in. A doorway is at the door, a wall is on the wall, and the inside of a room is in the room.

examples: I'll meet you at the station.
The keys are in the drawer.
There is a map on the wall.
She left her bag on the bus.
entries.pattern: at a point · in a space · on a surface
entries.example: I'll meet you at the station.
entries.contrast: at the door · in the room · on the wall

question.zh-Hans: 去、进、离开，介词该怎么配？
question.zh-Hant: 去、進、離開，介詞該怎麼配？
question.en: Which preposition marks going, entering or leaving?

summary.zh-Hans: to 朝目的地，into 进入空间，onto 到表面上，from 表示起点，out of 和 off 表示离开。arrive、reach、go home 各有自己的搭配。
summary.zh-Hant: to 朝目的地，into 進入空間，onto 到表面上，from 表示起點，out of 和 off 表示離開。arrive、reach、go home 各有自己的搭配。
summary.en: To marks a destination, into movement into a space, onto movement onto a surface, and from a starting point. Arrive, reach and go home have their own patterns.

usage.zh-Hans:
go to the office、walk into the hall、put the cup onto the tray、come from the station、get out of the car、take the bag off the chair。through 强调从内部穿过，across 强调从一边到另一边。into 和 onto 把“进入”说得更明确；日常英语里 put it in the box 也很普通。

arrive in 用于城市或国家，arrive at 用于建筑物、车站等较小地点，不用 arrive to。reach the station 不加 to。home、here、there 前通常不加 to：go home、come here。enter the room 已经包含进入，普通用法不必再加 into；enter into an agreement 是另一个固定说法。
usage.zh-Hant:
go to the office、walk into the hall、put the cup onto the tray、come from the station、get out of the car、take the bag off the chair。through 強調從內部穿過，across 強調從一邊到另一邊。into 和 onto 把“進入”說得更明確；日常英語裡 put it in the box 也很普通。

arrive in 用於城市或國家，arrive at 用於建築物、車站等較小地點，不用 arrive to。reach the station 不加 to。home、here、there 前通常不加 to：go home、come here。enter the room 已經包含進入，普通用法不必再加 into；enter into an agreement 是另一個固定說法。
usage.en:
Say go to the office, walk into the hall, put the cup onto the tray, come from the station, get out of the car and take the bag off the chair. Through stresses movement inside something; across stresses movement from one side to the other. Into and onto make the movement explicit, while put it in the box is also ordinary.

Arrive in is for a city or country, and arrive at is for a building, station or similar point. Do not say arrive to. Reach the station has no to. Home, here and there normally take no to: go home, come here. Enter the room already includes the movement, so into is unnecessary in that ordinary use. Enter into an agreement is a separate fixed phrase.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 arrive to the station 或 go to home。到达是 arrive at/in，回家是 go home。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 arrive to the station 或 go to home。到達是 arrive at/in，回家是 go home。
pitfall.en: Avoid arrive to the station and go to home. Use arrive at or arrive in, and say go home.

examples: We walked into the hall.
She arrives in Paris on Monday.
Take the bag off the chair.
I went home after the meeting.
entries.pattern: to a destination · into a space · from a source
entries.example: We walked into the hall.
entries.contrast: go to the office · go home · arrive at the office

question.zh-Hans: 几个形容词叠在名词前，哪个在前？
question.zh-Hant: 幾個形容詞疊在名詞前，哪個在前？
question.en: Which adjective comes first before a noun?

summary.zh-Hans: 名词前常见的顺序是观点、大小、年龄、形状、颜色、来源、材料、用途。一次不要堆太多形容词。
summary.zh-Hant: 名詞前常見的順序是觀點、大小、年齡、形狀、顏色、來源、材料、用途。一次不要堆太多形容詞。
summary.en: Before a noun, the usual order is opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, then purpose. Do not stack many adjectives at once.

usage.zh-Hans:
a lovely small old round table 比 a old small lovely table 自然。限定词和数量在最前：those two lovely chairs。材料紧挨名词：a red wooden box。用途像名词一样贴着中心名词：a leather walking shoe。这个顺序是倾向，不是数学公式；母语者靠听起来顺不顺来判断。

同一类、可以互换的形容词之间有时加逗号：a cold, wet day。固定顺序里的不同类别通常不加逗号。写作时两三个形容词通常足够。不确定时，把最主观的评价放得离名词更远。
usage.zh-Hant:
a lovely small old round table 比 a old small lovely table 自然。限定詞和數量在最前：those two lovely chairs。材料緊挨名詞：a red wooden box。用途像名詞一樣貼著中心名詞：a leather walking shoe。這個順序是傾向，不是數學公式；母語者靠聽起來順不順來判斷。

同一類、可以互換的形容詞之間有時加逗號：a cold, wet day。固定順序裡的不同類別通常不加逗號。寫作時兩三個形容詞通常足夠。不確定時，把最主觀的評價放得離名詞更遠。
usage.en:
A lovely small old round table sounds natural, while a old small lovely table does not. Determiners and numbers come first: those two lovely chairs. Material sits next to the noun: a red wooden box. A purpose behaves like part of the noun: a leather walking shoe. The order is a strong tendency, not a formula.

Commas can separate adjectives of the same type that could swap places: a cold, wet day. Adjectives in the fixed order normally need no comma. Two or three adjectives are usually enough. If you are unsure, put the most personal opinion farthest from the noun.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 a red big car。大小通常在颜色前：a big red car。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 a red big car。大小通常在顏色前：a big red car。
pitfall.en: Avoid a red big car. Size normally comes before colour: a big red car.

examples: They bought a lovely small old table.
She carried a big red wooden box.
Those two new Italian chairs are uncomfortable.
It was a cold, wet day.
entries.pattern: opinion + size + age + shape + colour + origin + material + noun
entries.example: They bought a lovely small old table.
entries.contrast: a big red car · a red big car

question.zh-Hans: 最高级怎么构成，前面要不要 the？
question.zh-Hant: 最高級怎麼構成，前面要不要 the？
question.en: How do I form a superlative, and when do I add the?

summary.zh-Hans: 短形容词常用 the + -est，长形容词常用 the most。最高级通常要有比较范围，one of the 后面用复数名词。
summary.zh-Hant: 短形容詞常用 the + -est，長形容詞常用 the most。最高級通常要有比較範圍，one of the 後面用複數名詞。
summary.en: Short adjectives often take the + -est, and longer ones the most. A superlative normally has a range, and one of the is followed by a plural noun.

usage.zh-Hans:
tallest、simplest 这类短词用 -est；expensive、careful 用 the most。good、bad、far 的最高级是 best、worst、farthest 或 furthest。名词前通常有 the：the oldest building in the town。范围用 in 接地点，用 of 接一组：the best of the three。人生经历的最高级常接现在完成时：the best meal I've had。

不要同时用 most 和 -est。one of the best player 是错的，因为 one of 后面是复数：one of the best players。most people 表示“大多数”，不是最高级；最高级是 the most useful of the three。作表语时 the 有时可以省，但名词前的最高级通常保留 the。
usage.zh-Hant:
tallest、simplest 這類短詞用 -est；expensive、careful 用 the most。good、bad、far 的最高級是 best、worst、farthest 或 furthest。名詞前通常有 the：the oldest building in the town。範圍用 in 接地點，用 of 接一組：the best of the three。人生經歷的最高級常接現在完成時：the best meal I've had。

不要同時用 most 和 -est。one of the best player 是錯的，因為 one of 後面是複數：one of the best players。most people 表示“大多數”，不是最高級；最高級是 the most useful of the three。作表語時 the 有時可以省，但名詞前的最高級通常保留 the。
usage.en:
Short adjectives such as tallest and simplest take -est. Longer ones such as expensive and careful take the most. The superlatives of good, bad and far are best, worst, and farthest or furthest. A noun normally has the: the oldest building in the town. Use in for a place and of for a group: the best of the three. A life-experience superlative often takes the present perfect: the best meal I've had.

Do not combine most with -est. One of the best player is wrong because one of takes a plural: one of the best players. Most people means the majority, not a superlative. The superlative is the most useful of the three. The can sometimes drop when the superlative is predicative, but it normally stays before a noun.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 the most tallest，也不要写 one of the best player。用 the tallest，或 one of the best players。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 the most tallest，也不要寫 one of the best player。用 the tallest，或 one of the best players。
pitfall.en: Avoid the most tallest and one of the best player. Say the tallest, or one of the best players.

examples: This is the oldest building in the town.
It was the most useful of the three maps.
She is one of the best players in the club.
That is the best meal I've had here.
entries.pattern: the + -est · the most + adjective · one of the + superlative + plural
entries.example: This is the oldest building in the town.
entries.contrast: the tallest building · the most useful map

question.zh-Hans: “这么……”用 so 还是 such？
question.zh-Hant: “這麼……”用 so 還是 such？
question.en: Do I use so or such for this kind of emphasis?

summary.zh-Hans: so 后面接形容词或副词；such 后面接名词短语。such a 和 so + 形容词 + a 都可以强调单数可数名词。
summary.zh-Hant: so 後面接形容詞或副詞；such 後面接名詞短語。such a 和 so + 形容詞 + a 都可以強調單數可數名詞。
summary.en: So is followed by an adjective or adverb. Such is followed by a noun phrase. Both such a and so + adjective + a can emphasise a singular count noun.

usage.zh-Hans:
so tired、so quickly 修饰的是形容词或副词。such a long day、such nice people、such weather 修饰的是名词短语。单数可数名词两种都对：such a cold day，或较正式的 so cold a day。数量用 so，不用 such：so many people、so much time、so few seats。

结果从句是 so tired that she left，或 such a long day that she left。不要把 so 直接放在 a + 名词前。such 本身不是形容词，不能说 the weather is such cold。
usage.zh-Hant:
so tired、so quickly 修飾的是形容詞或副詞。such a long day、such nice people、such weather 修飾的是名詞短語。單數可數名詞兩種都對：such a cold day，或較正式的 so cold a day。數量用 so，不用 such：so many people、so much time、so few seats。

結果從句是 so tired that she left，或 such a long day that she left。不要把 so 直接放在 a + 名詞前。such 本身不是形容詞，不能說 the weather is such cold。
usage.en:
So tired and so quickly modify an adjective or adverb. Such a long day, such nice people and such weather modify a noun phrase. A singular count noun allows both: such a cold day, or the more formal so cold a day. Quantities take so, not such: so many people, so much time, so few seats.

The result patterns are so tired that she left and such a long day that she left. Do not put so directly before a plus a noun. Such is not an adjective, so the weather is such cold is not English.

pitfall.zh-Hans: 不要写 so a long day 或 such tired。名词短语用 such a long day；单独的形容词用 so tired。
pitfall.zh-Hant: 不要寫 so a long day 或 such tired。名詞短語用 such a long day；單獨的形容詞用 so tired。
pitfall.en: Avoid so a long day and such tired. A noun phrase takes such a long day; a bare adjective takes so tired.

examples: She was so tired that she left.
It was such a long day that she left.
I didn't expect so many people.
They served such nice bread.
entries.pattern: so + adjective / adverb · such + noun phrase
entries.example: She was so tired that she left.
entries.contrast: so tired · such a long day · so many people

question.zh-Hans: 还、已经、尚未，用 still、already 还是 yet？
question.zh-Hant: 還、已經、尚未，用 still、already 還是 yet？
question.en: Still, already, or yet?

summary.zh-Hans: still 表示情况仍在继续；already 表示比预期更早；yet 多用于否定句和疑问句，表示到目前为止。
summary.zh-Hant: still 表示情況仍在繼續；already 表示比預期更早；yet 多用於否定句和疑問句，表示到目前為止。
summary.en: Still means a situation continues. Already means earlier than expected. Yet, mainly in negatives and questions, means up to now.

usage.zh-Hans:
She is still in the lab 表示没有离开。I've already eaten 表示吃饭早于对方的预期。Have you eaten yet? 和 I haven't eaten yet 把截止点放在现在。still 放在主要动词前或 be 后；否定里常用 still not：I still haven't started。already 可在句中或句末。yet 通常在句末。

肯定句里表示“已经”不用 yet。yet 放在句首时常常是“然而”，和完成体无关：The room is small. Yet it is bright。中文“了”不能自动决定用 already 还是过去时；already 强调早于预期。
